subject: maths
question: A Person travelled a distance of 150 km and then returned to the starting point. The time taken for the outward journey was 2(1)/(2) hours more than that for the return journey. His speed for the return journey was 10 km/h more than that for the outward journey. His speed for the return journey, in km/h, was:
solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 150 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let, the speed of outward journey = x km/h

So, the speed of return journey = (x + 10) km/h

Then, 150/x - 150/(x + 10) = 2(1)/(2)

⇒ (150(x+10)-150x)/(x(x+10))=(5)/(2)

⇒ (150x+1500-150x)/(x(x+10))=(5)/(2)

⇒ (1500)/(x²+10x)=(5)/(2)

⇒ (300)/(x²+10x)=(1)/(2)

⇒ x² + 10x = 600

⇒ x2 + 10x - 600 = 0

⇒ x2 + 30x - 20x - 600 = 0

⇒ x (x + 30) - 20 (x + 30) = 0

⇒ (x - 20) (x + 30) = 0

⇒ x - 20 = 0 ⇒ x = 20

⇒ x + 30 = 0 ⇒ x = - 30 ("-" will be naglated)

∴ The speed of the return journey = (20 + 10) km/h = 30 km/h

**∴ The person's speed for the return journey, in km/h, was 30 km/h**
